title: Interval Push Conditioning
description: Players push the width of the court repeatedly within a time limit, then rest for a fixed interval, a simple and measurable conditioning staple.

content.objective: Build conditioning through simple, measurable push intervals with controlled rest.
content.setup: Players line up on the sideline with a timer set for repeated intervals.
instructions: On the whistle, push width-to-width across the court, counting each crossing.
Complete as many crossings as possible within a set time (for example, 45 seconds).
Rest for a fixed interval, then repeat for the planned number of rounds.
Track the crossing count each round to measure fatigue across the set.
coachingPoints: Keep a consistent pace rather than sprinting hard early and fading late.
Touch each sideline clearly before turning back.
Use the rest interval fully to recover, not to chat or wander.
commonMistakes: Cutting the turn short instead of touching the sideline.
Pacing conservatively instead of pushing at genuine effort.
Letting technique break down once fatigue sets in.
content.safety: Build up to this conditioning level gradually; stop if a player shows signs of overheating or distress.
